A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SafeVLA/ISA study and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–H. The retained material can be matched reliably despite additions and renumbering in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulation experiments, including Safety-CHORES comparisons, ablations, robustness tests, and appendix correlation analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original generalization, perturbation, optimizer, and training-dynamics results, plus a qualitative physical-robot deployment study.

M1.justification: The core ISA formulation, losses, and original safety predicates remain unchanged. Section 5.3 adds deployment adaptations involving pose-based perception, separated policy and motor control, and simulator calibration; Appendix B.7 also evaluates alternative Lagrangian optimizers.

E1.justification: v3 adds DivScene evaluation across six scene categories, a physical Safety-PickUp scenario, and instruction and image corruptions beyond the retained color, lighting, and material perturbations. These substantially broaden the evaluated environments and input conditions.

E2.justification: Table 11 adds evaluated PID-Lagrangian and Augmented-Lagrangian alternatives on the three original tasks. Table 1 retains the same SPOC variants, FLaRe, FLaRe-RS, and Poliformer comparators.

E3.justification: New protocols include zero-shot scoring under five GPT-4-discovered predicates, measuring their overlap with original predicates, and semantic/perceptual and physical-deployment tests. The original splits, 600-step limit, SR/CC metrics, and 15M/25M training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices B.4–B.8 add unseen-predicate generalization and coverage analysis, per-constraint cost breakdowns, semantic/perceptual robustness tests, alternative-optimizer experiments, and training-dynamics analysis. The original elicitation, penalty, threshold, and extreme-failure studies are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A retains the same correlation tests, p-values, and 1% significance threshold. v3 introduces no repeated-run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their values, while Tables 6–11 add substantial results. For example, new DivScene results report average SR/CC of 0.39/1.0 for ISA and 0.37/10.5 for FLaRe. v3 also adds training trajectories and qualitative physical-deployment findings.

T1.justification: The CMDP formulation, mathematical safety predicates, Equations 1–10, and Algorithms 1–5 are retained. The added explanation connecting instantaneous and cumulative costs does not change the mathematics; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The ISA and Safety-CHORES contributions, novelty claim, and headline 83.58% safety improvement and +3.85% task-performance claims remain unchanged. The abstract specifies metrics and mobile-manipulation scope already explained in v2.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning generalizable safety logic, predicate representativeness, balanced risk reduction, and constraint-enforcement dynamics. Section 5.3 introduces a physical-transfer interpretation, while Appendix G expands discussion of binary severity, credit assignment, risk-sensitive objectives, and the continuing need for extensive physical validation.

D1.justification: Table 12 newly discloses the initial Lagrange multiplier of 0.001 and its learning rate of 0.035, and names OmniSafe alongside AllenAct. Section 5.3 adds robot hardware, perception, calibration, and deployment-pipeline details. Existing resource-access and licensing statements are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds supporting literature on newer VLAs and multimodal alignment, including Gemini Robotics and CoT-VLA, plus FoundationPose and DivScene. It briefly distinguishes open-ended VLAs from fixed-task SafeRL agents, while retaining its central positioning relative to FLaRe, GRAPE, and constrained learning.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section ordering remain intact. Local revisions include clearer abstract wording, expanded background and setup explanations, rewritten limitations, an explanatory pipeline paragraph in B.9, and author, conference, and acknowledgement updates.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the displayed evidence with six analysis tables, a physical-platform figure, and a three-panel training-dynamics figure. Existing displays are retained with relocation and renumbering, and the hyperparameter table gains two rows.

improvement.justification: The new generalization tests, optimizer diagnostics, deployment study, and multiplier settings improve empirical support and reproducibility. The gain is limited by the qualitative physical evaluation and inconsistencies in new results: Table 6 reports FLaRe component costs summing to 8.150 but a total of 11.140.
